sentences.review: This is the first time 'dir' appears, but it has no grammar note. The du/dich/dir concept (which even uses this sentence as an example) is only attached at entry 52; consider attaching 'pronoun.personal.du_dich_dir' here and setting first_entry to 51.

sentences.text: Ist Ziri mit dir in Berlin?
sentences.en: Is Ziri in Berlin with you?

sentences.text: Und wie ist es mit dir?

sentences.review: 'Kann ich mit dir?' sounds incomplete; natives would say 'Kann ich mit dir mit?' (or just 'Kann ich mit?'), so consider replacing or rephrasing it.
sentences.notes: The verb of motion is left out, as is common with modal verbs.

sentences.text: Gut, dass Leanna mit dir hier ist.
sentences.en: Good thing Leanna is here with you.

sentences.text: Sie ist heute mit dir in Wien, nicht mit mir.
sentences.en: She's in Vienna with you today, not with me.

sentences.notes: Typical reply to a wish such as 'Have a nice day!'
